reasoning_checks: Capitalization requires recognition and eligible cost evidence; purchase cash, resource measurement and periodic expense are separated. Significant components/replacements are distinguished from routine maintenance without inventing a generalized standards engine.

Historical cost, accumulated depreciation and impairment are reconciled separately. Both contra balances are credit-normal asset reductions, not cash reserves or liabilities. Disposal removes all related accounts.

Straight-line and usage allocation are derived with nonnegative costs/residual, positive life/output denominators and explicit elapsed/use domains. Zero elapsed, residual above carrying amount and usage beyond the initial estimate are addressed. Depreciation is a period cost only under the service-case assumptions; other-asset absorption is explicitly acknowledged.
The revised remaining-life calculation is prospective, based on new information. It is distinguished from a prior-period error and a change of measurement basis.

Recoverable amount uses the higher supplied sale/use route after depreciation; no automatic cost-model write-up. Independently assessable cash inflows are assumed; CGU valuation and goodwill allocation are outside scope. Reversal requires changed estimates and the hypothetical no-impairment carrying ceiling; passage of time alone and goodwill are excluded.

Alder sale control transfer and both cash settlements occur on 30 June 2027 after six months of depreciation. Gross receipt and fee remain visible; the arithmetic net is not a universal permission to net real statement presentation.

The lifecycle identity D+J-g=C-S is derived algebraically and checked against independent journals; unchanged proceeds imply timing changes cannot change undiscounted final profit in the closed case. This does not validate classification or imply no tax/valuation consequences.

Finite-life intangibles begin amortization at availability; legal and economic limits, indefinite-life reassessment, six development criteria and the no-reinstatement boundary are explicit. Research and pre-eligibility expense are not silently capitalized.

Investment property is distinguished by use from owned operating property and ordinary-course inventory. Cost/fair-value examples have fixed policies and supplied reliable valuation. Financial-claim amortized-cost eligibility is stipulated, not asserted for every investment; the effective-interest recursion is derived from fixed cash flows.

Economic depreciation uses constant-rate unchanged-information present values; its capital-recovery/return identity is derived. A news example distinguishes unexpected price change from physical wear or systematic cost allocation.

Every exercise prompt was manually matched to its full solution, including units, partial periods, current versus cumulative profit, separate asset entries and evidence boundaries. The checker verifies arithmetic, not prose by proxy.

limitations: Synthetic fixed-calendar cases; no empirical useful-life, fair-value or impairment estimate is validated.
Exact identities and independent journals support, but do not replace, the written recognition and source-scope audit.
Selected dated AASB/IAS method conventions, not a complete or universally current accounting standard.
No browser, mobile or print visual QA.
Author audit is not external academic, professional or jurisdiction-specific certification.

Real recognition, life, fair-value and impairment estimates need documentary evidence and the applicable reporting-date standard. Construction, taxes, leases, revaluation, held-for-sale accounting and complex financial assets are outside this chapter’s case scope.
Visual browser/mobile/print QA remains pending under the standing local-preview restriction. No attempt to circumvent it was made.
